messages.subject: Re: [R-sig-DB] How to write to database schema other than public using RPostgreSQL
messages.subject_clean: How to write to database schema other than public using RPostgreSQL
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

Since so many inquiry on schema access have been received,
I have made a trial implementation and committed to the svn repository
as r176.

Pleasy try to use c("schema", "table") to the place where you want to  
refer "schema"."table".

The modification of the code is kept very minimal just add an option  
of collapse="." to paste
in comparison to the postgresqlQuoteId.  However since this function  
was used to quote vector
and return the quoted vector for the table definition construction,  
the new function was made
under a different name, as "postgresqlTableRef".  This name might not  
be optimal as this can
be also used for "table"."column" structure construction.  If any  
better name is proposed,
I will change.

Although some brief tests have been done, I personally do not depend  
on schema now and
there might be shortcomings.  So, don't hesitate to tell me if  
something is wrong.

Sincerely,
-- 
Tomoaki NISHIYAMA

Advanced Science Research Center,
Kanazawa University,
13-1 Takara-machi,
Kanazawa, 920-0934, Japan

messages.subject_clean: Problem - R postgresql install in windows - fatal error with libpq-fe.h
messages.body_plain:
Hi Emmanuel,

> I am trying to compile the package RPostgreSQL from source (in  
> Windows), but I have a message error, dealing with the libpq-fe.h  
> file. I added snapshot of the command error message.
> Thanks a lot in advance if you can give me advice about how to  
> solve this issue and installing the package.


The message looks like that the compiler cannot find the include file  
which is
required to develop a program connecting postgresql through libpq.

So, the problem seems to reside how and where you installed PostgreSQL.

The include file search path given with -I option is perhaps not a  
standard one?
Is the directory "C:\Program FilesPostgreSQL\8.4"/include
a correct one? (Note there is no speparator between "Files" and  
"PostgreSQL")
Do you set this path as some environmental variable?

> I added snapshot of the command error message.


A copy as text is preferred (if it is possible).

Perhaps you can get more information if you explain exactly how you  
installed
R and PostgreSQL, both of which are required for RPostgreSQL.
-- 
Tomoaki NISHIYAMA

Advanced Science Research Center,
Kanazawa University,
13-1 Takara-machi,
Kanazawa, 920-0934, Japan

I have PostgreSQL 8.4 on Linux. 
I want to install RPostgreSQL on the Windows version of R.
When I choose "Packages" and "Install Package(s)" I do not find RPostgreSQL 
in the list of available packages.
I can find RODBC and the older RpgSQL in the list.
My repositories are CRAN, CRAN extras, and R-forge.

RGUI also gives an option to install via a .zip file. But the CRAN R page 
only has the .tar.gz file.

Am I missing something ?

We all are missing a volunteer to maintain the binary Windows packages for 32
and 64 bit.

Building this on Windows requires building PostgreSQL first. That is too much
too ask for from CRAN, and as nobody else has done, you have no volunteer
labour to profit from.

So source it is for now, which explains why you do not see it in a list of
handily prepared _binary_ packages.

Hope this helps,  Dirk
